extracted.intended_audience: researchers in theoretical mathematics, theoretical physics, and theoretical computer science applying for Simons Foundation Targeted Grants (MPS)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and process for Simons Foundation Targeted Grants in Mathematics and Physical Sciences, aimed at supporting high-risk projects of exceptional promise in theoretical math, physics, and theoretical computer science. Covers LOI review, quality-based applicant criteria, collaboration impact expectations, and Simons Investigator selection characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program focus / eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The division's primary focus is on theoretical mathematics, theoretical physics, and theoretical computer science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted Grants in MPS are intended to support projects within these theoretical areas; applicants should align proposals with this disciplinary focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for high-risk, high-reward work
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended to support high-risk projects of exceptional promise and scientific importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program explicitly favors risky projects that, if successful, would have exceptional scientific importance; proposals should emphasize novelty and potential transformational impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI stage — suitability and novelty assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter of Intent (LOI) stage assesses suitability and novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are recommended to submit an LOI if they believe their research meets the RFA criteria; a favorable LOI review may lead to invitation to submit a full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of previous research
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and significance of the applicant's previous research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the applicant's past work for rigor, impact, and relevance as an indicator of ability to succeed on the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential impact on future research
rubrics_metrics.description: Likely impact the grant will have on future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment considers how the funded work would influence subsequent research directions, open new areas, or catalyze advances in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication record in high-quality journals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong record of publications in leading journals is used as evidence of research quality and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship and trainees
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant's current and recent Ph.D. students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider the applicant's role in training and mentoring graduate students as part of overall research leadership and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research activity and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant's travel goals and general research activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans for collaboration, travel, and active engagement with the research community are considered indicators of how the grant will be used to advance work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration addresses fundamental scientific importance
rubrics_metrics.description: A collaboration should address a mathematical or theoretical topic of fundamental scientific importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborations are expected to focus on deep, foundational problems rather than incremental or narrowly applied topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of a novel area or new direction
rubrics_metrics.description: A significant, new development creates a novel area for exploration or provides a new direction for progress in an established field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate how the collaboration will enable new lines of inquiry or redirect progress in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and type of scientific questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The questions addressed by the collaboration may be concrete or conceptual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both concrete technical problems and broad conceptual questions are acceptable, but they should be clearly stated and motivated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformative potential / milestone importance
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be little doubt that answering them would constitute a major scientific milestone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for compelling arguments that resolving the posed questions would represent a major advance or milestone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined initial activities and measurable goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The project should have clearly defined initial activities and goals by which progress and success can be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborations must include concrete early-stage plans and metrics for assessing progress; this helps reviewers gauge feasibility and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Investigator — track record and promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection focuses on track record of accomplishment and continued promise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simons Investigators are chosen based on past achievements and evidence they will continue to produce significant theoretical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Investigator — support characteristics (stable, no specific deliverables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outstanding theoretical scientists who receive a stable base of research support; Tier-1 senior investigator status with no specific deliverables, allowing risk-taking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigator awards provide flexible, sustained support designed to enable high-risk research rather than enforce specific short-term deliverables.
